title: Analysis by LC-MS/MS of polar pesticides in fruits and vegetables using new hybrid stationary phase
author: Cutillas, R. Fernández-Alba

steps.title: Configure LC system and gradient
steps.instruction: Install a Restek Raptor Polar column (2.7 µm, 50 × 2.1 mm) and a guard column cartridge (2.7 µm, 5 × 2.1 mm) in an EXP Direct Connect Holder on a Shimadzu Nexera UC. Prepare mobile phase A as water containing 0.5 % formic acid and mobile phase B as acetonitrile containing 0.5 % formic acid (formic‑acid percentages tested: 0, 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 1 %; 0.5 % gives optimal peak shape). Set column oven to 35 °C and the total flow to 0.6 mL min⁻¹. Program the gradient: start at 35 % A, increase linearly to 90 % A at 2 min, hold isocratically until 9 min, then decrease linearly to 35 % A at 10 min and hold for 2 min for re‑equilibration.

steps.title: Set mass spectrometer parameters
steps.instruction: Connect the LC to a Shimadzu triple‑quadrupole 8060 equipped with an electrospray ionization (ESI) source. Set the interface temperature to 300 °C, the desolvation line (DL) temperature to 200 °C (or 400 °C when the heat block is used), and the interface voltage to 3 kV. Adjust gas flows to: nebulizer 3 L min⁻¹, heating gas 10 L min⁻¹, drying gas 10 L min⁻¹. Add the internal standard 13C¹⁵N‑glyphosate. Manually optimize each pesticide by precursor‑ion search and define an acquisition window of ±0.5 min for every analyte. Apply the compound‑specific MS parameters listed in Table 1.

substeps.instruction:

- Fosetyl: RT 9.73 min, precursor m/z 410, CE1 9, SRM1 148, CE2 12, SRM2 363
- Glufosinate: RT 2.66 min, precursor m/z 180, CE1 0, SRM1 133, CE2 63, SRM2 185
- Glyphosate: RT 5.78 min, precursor m/z 167, CE1 9, SRM1 20, CE2 63, SRM2 1479
- Glyphosate C13N15: RT 5.76 min, precursor m/z 171, CE1 25, SRM1 71, CE2 63, SRM2 337

steps.title: Validate method with matrix‑matched calibrations
steps.instruction: Prepare matrix‑matched calibration curves for tomato, onion, quince and orange using extracts (water/methanol 1:1, no dilution). Spike each matrix at five concentration levels: 10, 20, 50, 100 and 500 µg kg⁻¹. Inject the standards and determine instrumental limits of quantification (LOQ) – observed between 10 and 50 µg kg⁻¹ – and the linear range for each analyte. Use weighted linear regression (1/x) and accept linearity when individual residuals are <20 % (exceptions: chlorate in tomato and perchlorate in all matrices lose linearity above 100 µg kg⁻¹). Calculate matrix effects by comparing the slope of each matrix‑matched curve with the slope obtained in pure solvent; classify effects as none (0‑20 %), low/medium (20‑50 %) or strong (>50 %). Record the LOQ, linear range and matrix‑effect percentage for every compound in each matrix as shown in Table 2.
